meta: Dramas like Descendants of the Sun: five glossy romances built on uniforms, crisis and two couples.
standfirst: A special forces captain, a surgeon, a fictional war zone, and a romance conducted almost entirely under threat of death. The scale is the appeal here: the money is on screen, the second couple is better written than the first, and the plot exists to keep putting the leads in danger. These five give you that, and we are honest about which ones have more underneath.

picks.why: Same director, and the half of this show that actually worked. Yoo In Shik shot both, and this is the disaster-medicine half of Descendants extended into twenty episodes: mass casualties, impossible operations, a surgeon who chose principle over a career. Difference: the romance is secondary rather than the product, and the writing is a great deal better.

Same writer, doing the serious version. Kim Eun Sook again on love, uniform and the cost of serving something larger than yourself, with the same taste for grand declarations and enormous production. Difference: it is a tragedy about the end of a country, so the gloss carries real weight and the ending will not comfort you.

Glossy action romance with a bodyguard at the centre. Same pleasures: choreographed fights, a man who is very good at violence protecting someone who is not, a political conspiracy in the background. Difference: the romance is much weaker and the politics much nastier, so the balance tips toward the action.

For the uncomplicated star romance. If what you wanted was two beautiful people, a warm tone and a plot that never seriously threatens them, this is the same product in Joseon dress. Difference: no military, no medical crisis, and the back half sags once the political plot takes over.

The other big-budget SBS disaster investigation. A crash, a cover-up, action shot abroad at genuine film scale, and Bae Suzy again in the middle of it. Difference: no romance to speak of and no comfort, and it stops on a cliff rather than ending, so go in for the set pieces.

against.title: Goblin
against.why: The standard pairing, on the grounds of the same writer and the same year. It is a fantasy melodrama about immortality and memory, built on longing rather than jeopardy. The Descendants pleasure, banter under fire, is not in it.

against.title: Crash Landing on You
against.why: Paired constantly because both are romances across a military line. But that one is a comedy with an ensemble and a village, and its danger is bureaucratic. This is a two-hander about people who might die tomorrow, and the tones do not transfer.

against.title: Uncontrollably Fond
against.why: Recommended on cast and gloss, and it is a terminal-illness melodrama with a completely different contract. Descendants threatens death constantly and delivers it rarely. This one tells you the ending in the first episode and makes you sit through it.
